source.title: Patch-Effect Graph Kernels for LLM Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies patch-effect graph representations on IOI and cites the original IOI circuit, but does not test the claimed 26-head circuit, its head classes, or the versions' claims about its faithfulness or generality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many graph-classification accuracies, but these classify corruption or task slices; they do not measure IOI completion performance or the claimed circuit's faithfulness, completeness, or minimality. Those accuracies are therefore not recorded as rows. Table 10 reports paired-patching results for screened residual-stream candidate edges; these are recorded as related IOI patching results, not as tests of the claimed head circuit.
record.test_reason: The paper uses GPT-2 small IOI as a testbed because its circuit is known, and reports only how well its own patch-effect graph pipeline classifies corruption slices. It patches residual-stream nodes, not attention heads, and never tests the 26-head circuit, its classes, backup heads, its generality or its faithfulness. It relies on the IOI finding as a tool rather than citing it only, so T4 fits better than the record's T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that patch-effect graphs compress slice-discriminative patching signal, with localized edge-slot features strongest. Raw-tensor and surface-cue controls are strong baselines. Screened DI only partially validates CI/PC edges, and task-general causal-circuit claims are explicitly out of scope.
record.recipe_differences: The paper constructs graphs from residual-stream patch-effect profiles using co-influence, partial correlation, or screened paired-patching measures, then evaluates graph representations and classifiers. It does not discover or ablate the original circuit's attention-head classes.
record.method_sensitivity: Graph construction and representation change classification results; prompt surface cues perform differently between the historical and surface-balanced IOI pairs. These are sensitivities of the paper's graph benchmark, not measured sensitivities of the claimed circuit's faithfulness or completeness.

fits_no_version.finding: Screened paired patching on GPT-2 small residual-stream nodes: top-CI and top-PC candidate edges had higher destination activation influence (0.373, 0.305) than random or low-rank CI screens (0.122, 0.102). Mediation and necessity were variable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlation-based patch-effect screens select residual-stream edges with stronger paired-patching activation influence than null screens on IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: Qualitative only: mean residual-stream patch effects concentrate in layers 5–10. In a 10-edge pilot, top edges sit at last-token layers 9–11, which the authors call consistent with the known IOI circuit. There are no head-level tests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream patching signal for IOI in GPT-2 small localizes to mid-to-late layers at the final token.

record.problems: The authors characterize the experiments as a controlled pilot. Their main binary comparisons use only two underlying slices; the screened direct-influence validation covers 10 paired prompts in one pilot and 50 held-out edges per candidate screen. Full direct-influence graph benchmarking is not performed. The paper also notes surface confounds in its historical IOI comparison and reports planned, rather than released, code.
record.rows_left_out: Graph-classification accuracies and associated representation/null-control results in Tables 2–9, plus the prompt-budget and bootstrap sensitivity results, were left out because they classify patch-derived slices or compare encodings rather than test IOI completion or the claimed head circuit. Table 1 reports heatmap color scales, not measured mean patch-effect values.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes and their roles, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality are all untested. Only residual-stream patching is done.
No ablation of name-mover heads and no test of backup or self-repair.
DistilGPT-2 is used only for graph-classification accuracy; head classes and roles are not examined in it, in other checkpoints, or in other tasks.
No comparison of whether other circuit-discovery methods, ablations or metrics recover the circuit.
The circuit's faithfulness and completeness are never evaluated under alternative ablations, metrics or distributions.
Corruption types vary, but the circuit's components are not tested across name orders, templates or numbers of names.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche are changed from cites_only/T6 to uses_without_test/T4: IOI and its known circuit serve as a controlled testbed, and only the study's own method's performance is reported. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head circuit, its seven classes and stated roles, and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality are not tested.
The paper does not ablate main name-mover heads or test self-repair by backup heads.
DistilGPT-2 is included in graph-representation experiments, but the paper does not test whether the claimed head classes and roles carry IOI in it, other checkpoints, or other tasks.
The paper compares graph-construction and representation choices, not whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover the claimed circuit.

The paper does not measure the claimed circuit's faithfulness or completeness under alternative ablations or prompt distributions. Its graph-classification and patching metrics are not evaluations of that circuit.
The paper varies IOI corruption types and includes other task families, but does not test the claimed head circuit across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

conditions.value: N = 100 per slice; discovery/evaluation split of 50 examples each

That is method-versus-method validation on residual-stream edges, not a measure of the IOI circuit. They arguably should not be rows; at most keep them as fits_no_version context.
